title: Add provenance-ledger and soft-repair scorer for targeted prompt-set rollbacks
author: Priya Shah
release_notes: Adds a provenance ledger (prompt-set snapshots + lineage) and a soft-repair scorer that surfaces targeted rollback candidates and severity-ranked repair suggestions. Integrates a CI hook to flag provenance drift and emit explainable failure reasons. No public API breaking changes.
body:
Motivation: CI noise from large prompt-set changes makes it hard to identify targeted fixes. This PR introduces a lightweight provenance ledger that captures prompt-set snapshots, hashes, and lineage metadata at eval time, plus a soft-repair scorer that ranks potential rollback or patch candidates by expected regression impact and repair confidence. The ledger enables fine-grained rollback decisions and gives humans an explainable trail for CI alerts.

What this changes: 1) provenance/ledger.py: ledger implementation (snapshot metadata, content hash, sample-level lineage references, minimal storage adapter interface). 2) scoring/soft_repair.py: candidate generation and severity-weighted scoring model (heuristic + lightweight ML ensemble). 3) hooks/ci_provenance_hook.py: CI hook that runs during eval CI, computes provenance drift score, emits structured explanation tokens to the CI log, and optionally marks the job as soft-fail (doesn't block merge but records an alert). 4) tests/*: unit + integration tests for ledger, scorer, and hook; includes a small replay fixture. 5) docs/eval/provenance.md and docs/ci/soft-fail-guidance.md. 6) .github/workflows/eval-ci.yaml: wire up the new hook as an eval check step (opt-in via EVAL_PROVENANCE=true).

Checklist: 
- [x] Ledger and adapter interface implemented
- [x] Soft-repair scorer with end-to-end tests
- [x] CI hook + workflow change (opt-in)
- [x] Documentation and quickstart for developers
- [x] Security review notes added (see security-comments in review thread)

Commits summary: 
- commit 1: bootstrap provenance ledger module + simple in-memory adapter
- commit 2: add soft-repair scorer prototype and candidate heuristics
- commit 3: add CI hook and runner integration with eval CI
- commit 4: unit tests for ledger and scorer; add replay fixtures
- commit 5: docs and quickstart; add examples of rollback workflow
- commit 6: polish; address reviewer feedback and tests flakiness

Files changed (high level): 
- provenance/ledger.py
- scoring/soft_repair.py
- hooks/ci_provenance_hook.py
- tests/provenance_test.py
- tests/soft_repair_test.py
- docs/eval/provenance.md
- docs/ci/soft-fail-guidance.md
- .github/workflows/eval-ci.yaml (small opt-in step)

Testing and CI: All unit and integration tests passed in the final runs. One flaky integration test (tests/soft_repair_test.py::test_candidate_rank_stability) failed on first run due to a seeded randomness issue; fixed by deterministically seeding the generator and re-ran. Linting and type checks passed. Security scanner initially flagged a potential prompt-storage exposure; mitigations added (redact-by-default + adapter uses configured store; docs updated to call out KMS/HSM guidance).

Review conversation (high level): 
- Marcus Chen: "Great direction — provenance will help a lot. A few questions about retention and PII; suggest defaulting to metadata-only storage and requiring explicit opt-in for storing prompt text."
  - Author reply: "Agreed — ledger defaults to metadata-only (hash + minimal lineage) and adapter interface enforces opt-in store for raw text. Added docs and tests."

- Ana López: "Soft-fail semantics are delicate for release engineers — can we make opt-in and add a dashboard signal rather than automatic Git blocking?"
  - Author reply: "Yes — CI hook is opt-in via EVAL_PROVENANCE env var; default behavior is to annotate and emit a failing annotation in CI but mark the job as soft-fail (non-blocking). Ops dashboards emit the alert and include suggested repair candidates. Docs updated with runbook."

- Jordan Kim (SRE): "What is the RPO for ledger in Dedicated/Private deployments? How does this behave in air-gapped installs?"
  - Author reply: "Ledger uses a swappable storage adapter. For air-gapped installs we include a filesystem adapter that stores encrypted snapshots by default. Added KMS integration notes and a short example for private installer."

Approval and merge: After addressing comments and adding deterministic seeds for the flaky test, reviewers approved. CI green on final run. Squash-merged into main on 2025-11-28.

Notes for maintainers: 
- The ledger storage adapter interface is intentionally minimal; if integrating with a long-term store, implement the adapter under provenance/adapters.
- The soft-repair scorer is intentionally conservative: it surfaces suggestions with a confidence score and a short explanation string to aid on-call triage. It does not auto-apply patches.
- The CI hook writes a short JSON blob to the CI artifacts directory (provenance-summary.json) which ops dashboards can pick up. By default the blob contains redacted examples and a pointer to the snapshot hash.

Follow-ups (tracked in ENG-4192): 
- Add a lightweight web UI to browse ledger snapshots and suggested repairs (spike planned).
- Evaluate ML-based candidate ranker for higher-signal workloads.
- Add an optional canary policy to auto-quarantine new prompt-set changes when provenance drift exceeds a threshold.

unit and integration tests + deterministic seeding fix
